steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been looking since your last treatment with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still smooth and happy with it, starting to come back a little, or pretty much back to how it was. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Happy With It
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

(Do not offer the touch-up yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: Starting to Come Back
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}, and you're right on time. The treatment starts wearing off around the three-month mark as the movement comes back. It's not the results failing. That's just how it works for everyone. Your notes say you were really happy with how it turned out. Does that sound right?

(Let them confirm. Stay warm. This is routine, not a problem.)

(Do not offer the touch-up yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Before
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and please don't feel bad. That's what happens when more time goes by between visits. The movement comes back, and the lines follow. It's easy to fix. Your notes say you were really happy with how it turned out. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. It's nothing they did wrong.)

(Do not offer the touch-up yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: One More Thing: Jaw Clenching
steps.content:
Perfect, you're all set for (day) at (time).

(If you already asked the jaw question during the file update, skip it. Confirm the appointment and end the call.)

One quick thing while I have you, {{contact_first_name}}. Have you noticed any jaw clenching, teeth grinding, or tension headaches?

(Let them answer.)

(If yes, read the next line.)

That's something we can often help with. It's the same treatment, just in the jaw muscles. I'll make a note so {{provider_name}} can take a look when you're in. No commitment, just worth a look.

(If no, read the next line.)

No problem. I always ask, because a lot of people don't know it's treatable. We'll see you (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}. Have a great day.

(Either way, end the call with the appointment confirmed.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file anyway. Can I ask you a few quick questions so it's up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the lines in a moment. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the area we treated. Have you noticed any of the lines starting to come back, even a little?

How about your skin in general, any dryness or sun spots bothering you?

Any jaw clenching, teeth grinding, or tension headaches?

Any big event coming up you'd want to look your best for?

Is there another treatment you've been curious about?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the lines coming back. When did you first start noticing them?

How about your skin in general, any dryness or sun spots bothering you?

Any jaw clenching, teeth grinding, or tension headaches?

Any big event coming up you'd want to look your best for?

Is there another treatment you've been curious about?

(Recap what you wrote down, including the lines, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between the lines and anything else you mentioned, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If the touch-up is the whole story, use the second button.)

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd like to feel good every time you catch your reflection. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Protect the Results
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is still looking the way you want it.

One thing before I let you go. It's been at least three months since your last visit. That's right about when things usually start to soften. The movement comes back slowly before the lines do, so you're usually the last one to notice. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes. If they hesitate, use the second button.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get your touch-up on the books now, just ahead of that. That way the results stay even and nobody sees the in-between stage. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let's find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Touch-Up Is the Whole Story: The Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, the nice thing is you already know what to expect. Getting back to that refreshed look is one visit away. If we catch it now, we're keeping up a result instead of starting over. That's the easiest version of this there is.

Let's get you back on the books. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it would last longer”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Most people hope it holds longer than it does.

Can I ask, how long did it hold before you saw the movement come back?

(Let them answer.)

Three to four months is typical, and it's the muscle waking back up, not the product failing. Some people run shorter, especially with strong muscles or a lot of exercise. That's useful to know, because timing and dose are the two things that change how long {{main_concern}} stays settled.

{{provider_name}} already has your notes, so this visit adjusts instead of guessing.

Would it help to know what would make it hold longer for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m thinking about fillers or something else”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. It might be the right call.

Can I ask what's caught your eye, and what you're hoping it does?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other treatment.)

They often work together. Botox handles the lines that come from movement. Filler and other treatments handle volume and texture. Which one fits {{main_concern}} depends on what's driving it, and that's a five-minute look, not a phone call. {{provider_name}} will tell you straight if the other treatment is the better fit.

Would it help to have that sorted out before you spend money on either?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a different injector, a deal somewhere else, or just waiting?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what would move {{main_concern}} for you. {{provider_name}} already knows how your face responds and what dose held, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the visit itself, or the thought of the full amount again?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

A lot of people don't realize this. Keeping up a result usually takes fewer units than starting over, and fewer units means less cost. When you come in, we go over how many units you'd need and what that costs, before anything is done. Nothing happens until you're happy with the numbers.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for a visit, or the worry about coming in every few months?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. A touch-up is quick to begin with, and we'll have everything ready when you walk in. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what spacing makes sense from there. Nobody is putting you on a schedule from the phone.

We'll fit that first visit around your day, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{main_concern}} specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at your face, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
